answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each new identity to lock a scarce token in escrow before it can earn trust. A verifier checks a signed cipher challenge at the network’s inlet, then releases the stake only after the agent completes a useful task without duplicating another identity’s work. Sybils can still appear, but each must tie up capital and risk losing it; an attacker who wants many trusted identities pays repeatedly, rather than minting them for free and letting them wander.
